bullets.title: META surges 7%+ on AI compute buildout; Ark buys, $1200 PT floated
bullets.body: META shares hit session highs up 7.3% after SemiAnalysis published a positive report on Meta's AI compute business. Meta confirmed its in-house 'Iris' AI chip enters production in September and plans to double compute to 14GW by 2027; Meta also began charging businesses for access to its AI models for the first time. Ark Invest bought 34,080 shares, and a Hedgeye-linked account floated a $1,200 target while multiple traders noted the market had previously assigned zero or negative value to Meta's AI capex. Separate ICML rumor circulated that Meta has an internal 'Mythos 5-level' model set to deploy within months.

bullets.title: Micron $250B US investment pledge; $MU projected to earn more in 2026 than past 35 years combined
bullets.body: Micron formally broke ground on its New York DRAM megafab in Clay, NY, and raised its total US manufacturing investment commitment to $250B through 2035. Fintwit accounts noted MU is on track to earn more in 2026 than the prior 35 combined years, with Wells Fargo raising its WDC target to $730 from $575 as a read-through. SK Hynix CEO separately warned the memory chip shortage could persist past 2030.

bullets.title: SK Hynix record $26.5B US ADR debut; opens 14-21% above $149 offer price
bullets.body: SK Hynix priced its Nasdaq ADR at $149 (raised 40 trillion won, down from 43 trillion), opened between $170 and $180, and briefly indicated as high as $181—a 14-21% premium. The deal surpassed Alibaba's 2014 IPO as the largest US equity offering by a foreign company. Leveraged 2x long (SKHX) and 1x short (SKHZ) ETFs announced for Tuesday launch. SK Group chairman signaled a 'much, much bigger' US investment plan and openness to building chip fabs on US soil. One fintwit account preferred MU for domestic memory exposure over SKHYV.

bullets.title: NVDA: Morgan Stanley NDR takeaways; unusual $5M put print; 50-DMA seen as gift
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's NVIDIA NDR noted the company has best visibility into global AI demand and expects the memory shortage to persist for several years—bullish for Rubin and HBM supply chains. One fintwit account flagged an unusual ~$5M short-dated NVDA put print as bearish positioning. A separate analyst called NVDA at its 50-day moving average 'still a damn gift.' NVIDIA is also prioritizing datacenter wafers over gaming, with Rubin margins cited at 'triple' consumer GeForce levels.

bullets.title: Fed semi-annual report: inflation elevated, AI/memory/chip prices cited; spring tick-up flagged
bullets.body: The Federal Reserve's semi-annual monetary policy report highlighted inflation remaining elevated, driven by tariffs, Middle East factors, and AI-related costs including memory and chip prices. Goldman Sachs separately estimated AI-induced memory, software, and electricity price increases are already adding 0.2%+ to YoY core PCE, rising to 0.5% by year-end. The report noted Q1 2026 growth was bolstered by high-tech investment and government spending; private credit vehicles faced notable Q1 redemption pressures. Asset valuations in stocks, corporate debt, and real estate trade above historic norms.

bullets.title: SPY gamma structure bullish: $3.5B call wall at 755, positive gamma; index 0.5% from ATH
bullets.body: Options flow showed billions in positive gamma at elevated SPY levels and a $3.5B call wall at the 755 strike. S&P 500 was 0.5% from an all-time high as of Thursday afternoon, with Nasdaq 100 erasing an earlier 0.8% drop to turn positive. SPX implied volatility fell to 10% for next week (8% for Monday)—the lowest term structure in 90+ days—while NDX IV held 20%, leaving little room for disappointment.

bullets.title: Rosenblatt defends optical/photonics: short sellers lack conviction, sector expected to 'smash earnings'
bullets.body: Rosenblatt argued that optical sector weakness over the last 1-2 months—attributed to CPO delay reports and China capacity fears—was overdone, and that short sellers 'have zero conviction and are preying on fear,' intending to cover ahead of earnings beats. Separately, a fintwit account noted photonics stocks including LITE, AAOI, AXTI, and COHR were testing three-month lows with bulls defending support but the bottom not yet confirmed. CPO volume readiness still requires integration and yield improvements.

bullets.title: LITE: InP capacity flagged as AI infrastructure bottleneck; VCSEL presentation at LightCounting July 15
bullets.body: A fintwit account noted Lumentum (LITE) had flagged InP capacity expansion on recent earnings calls, positioning InP as transitioning from an 'optics subtopic' to a critical physical AI infrastructure bottleneck. Lumentum's Oleg Shchekin is set to present on VCSEL-based wide-parallel optical interconnects for AI scale-up networks at LightCounting's virtual conference July 15. Google's coherent-lite transceiver (presented in 2021) is approaching volume adoption, and Meta is connecting campuses 2,000km apart using coherent optics—with Marvell DSP cited as a key enabler.

bullets.title: Memory prices up 4x in cycle; could rise another 2-3x but 85%+ gross margins unsustainable long-term
bullets.body: A detailed fintwit thread argued memory prices have risen roughly fourfold in the current cycle and could climb another two to three times, but that no commodity-like product can sustain margins above 85% for an extended period—setting an eventual price ceiling. Server DRAM spot prices continue rising per TrendForce, with long-term agreement caps limiting upside but supply remaining tight. AI infrastructure demand is broadening beyond hyperscalers to neoclouds, European data centers, sovereign compute, and enterprise coding.

bullets.title: 30-year Treasury yield hits 5.058%, highest since pre-GFC; market fragility index at ATH
bullets.body: The 30-year Treasury bond auction cleared at 5.058%, the highest level since the run-up to the Global Financial Crisis. UBS's proprietary market fragility index simultaneously hit an all-time high. Margin debt relative to GDP is now ~4.1%, the highest since 2000. Retail trader conviction is reportedly fading per Bloomberg. BofA sees net central bank hiking as a bearish macro signal for equities.

bullets.title: US permits UAE advanced computing imports without licenses; MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/ORCL named UK critical third parties
bullets.body: The US granted the UAE preferential export control terms, permitting import of advanced computing products without licenses. Separately, UK regulators (BoE, PRA, FCA) designated Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Oracle as critical third parties to the UK financial sector, beginning direct oversight July 13.

bullets.title: GOOGL: quarterly interest expense hits $500M, up 15x YoY on AI infrastructure financing
bullets.body: A fintwit account flagged that Google's quarterly interest expense exceeded $500 million, up 15x year-over-year, driven by funding its AI buildout. Hyperscaler capex and FCF consensus trackers covering AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, META, and ORCL are being updated at multiple discrete time points as forward estimates revise higher. Google is also scaling coherent-lite infrastructure at 2,000km campus-to-campus distances with Marvell DSP.

bullets.title: AI token price war hits OpenAI; AI firms double 2025 bond issuance pace; enterprise AI market seen at $155B by 2030
bullets.body: AI firms have already more than doubled all of 2025's bond sales in 2026, reflecting accelerating capital requirements. OpenAI is 'directly impacted' by a token price war as new frontier models trigger a race to the bottom. GPT-5.6 was announced as the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot and set a new ARC-AGI-3 SOTA of 7.8%. Apollo's $35B AI chip credit facility entered secondary market trading. Enterprise AI market is projected to exceed $155B by 2030.

bullets.title: Data center construction growth slowing; pipeline at 12-year backlog; electricity prices surging
bullets.body: Multiple fintwit accounts flagged that data center construction growth has 'slowed considerably,' while a separate account noted the data center project pipeline would take 12 years to clear at current build rates (up from 10), with 338 GW of projects queued. Goldman Sachs sees US electricity price surges 'just getting started' due to relentless data center demand, compounding the AI-driven PCE inflation discussed in the Fed report.

bullets.title: INTC: EMIB-T technology breaks AI/HPC scaling limits; CPU TAM seen at $200B+ by 2030 driven by OpenAI/Anthropic cloud deals
bullets.body: Intel's EMIB-T technology enables over 10x reticle dies in a single package with 12+ GT/s HBM4e support, targeting AI and HPC markets. A separate analyst models upside in Vera CPU TAM exceeding $200B by 2030, priced in high-single-digit thousands per unit, noting that OpenAI and Anthropic signing large cloud deals with Amazon, Google, and Microsoft is driving significant CPU catch-up demand after three years of AI chip deployment without corresponding CPU buildout.

bullets.title: CXMT sets July 16 subscription date for $4.3B Shanghai IPO; China helium export ban flagged
bullets.body: CXMT announced a July 16 subscription date for its $4.3B Shanghai IPO, emerging as a major Chinese memory semiconductor challenger. China separately imposed a temporary ban on helium exports, a critical input for semiconductor manufacturing and equipment cooling, a potential supply-chain disruption for US chipmakers.

bullets.title: BE: Scandium supply risk analyzed; primary equity risk is market capitalizing undeliverable 3-5GW trajectory
bullets.body: A detailed fintwit thread argued Bloom Energy faces a genuine strategic supply constraint from scandium sourcing, but available evidence does not confirm an imminent 2026 production stoppage. The primary equity risk is the market capitalizing a 3-5 GW volume trajectory that cannot actually be supplied. Scandium currently represents less than 1% of system revenue at current prices and output. Historical evidence suggests Chinese material has been part of the supply chain.

bullets.title: TSLA: robotaxi launch timing wouldn't move needle financially per Elon; TSLA down 10% YTD vs Nasdaq +16%
bullets.body: A fintwit bear account noted Tesla is down 10% YTD versus the Nasdaq's 16% gain and cited Elon's own admission that a one-year earlier robotaxi launch would not have materially affected financials. BYD now sells 2x the vehicles and makes 5x the batteries of Tesla. The account reported selling TSLA at $430 to avoid further losses.

bullets.title: Taiwan semiconductor exports +33% YoY in June; DRAM shipments surge 158% in H1 2026
bullets.body: Taiwan's semiconductor exports in June rose 33.4% YoY to $24.11B, with Q2 2026 chip exports up 43.7% YoY to $71.15B. H1 2026 totaled $133.17B, up 43.9% YoY. Most strikingly, DRAM chip exports surged 158.5% to $18.55B in H1 2026, confirming the memory supercycle thesis.

bullets.title: Japan PPI +7.1% YoY in June, fastest since early 2023; GPIF pushed toward domestic assets; yen surges
bullets.body: Japan's June PPI rose 7.1% YoY, beating the 6.8% forecast and accelerating from 6.3% prior—the fastest pace since early 2023. Finance Minister Katayama simultaneously pushed GPIF and households to increase domestic asset investment, sending USD/JPY down 0.5-0.6% to 161.40. 10-year JGB yields fell 10bps to 2.775% on the pivot. JPY shorts described as 'crowded at a time when conditions are shifting favorably.'
